root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit: Zeller Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Bf5

overview: White offers a pawn for development and the f-file; Black meets 3.Nc3 with 3...Bf5 and, after 4.f3 exf3 5.Qxf3, retreats the bishop to c8 or goes ...Nf6 and ...e6. White aims for fast development, Bc4/Bf4 and a kingside attack; Black consolidates the extra pawn and trades down. Most club games are open and tactical.

white_ideas.idea: Regain activity with f3 and Qxf3, hitting f7/b7
Develop Bc4, Bf4, Nge2 and castle quickly
Use the half-open f-file and g4/h4 pushes against the kingside

black_ideas.idea: Develop the bishop actively with ...Bf5 and keep the extra pawn
Return to ...e6 and ...Nf6 and trade pieces

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White d4 against Black missing the e-pawn
White pawn deficit offset by lead in development

character.notes: The Zeller is a mutual-attack line: White sacrifices a pawn and attacks, Black must avoid early traps on f7, b7 and the e-file.

gambit.notes: White gives the e-pawn; Black can keep it with ...exf3 or ...dxe4.

soundness.notes: Engine and master opinion on the BDG as a whole is that compensation is not enough; Black has the Zeller 3...Bf5 as a sound-looking route.

structure.notes: Centre opens at once: e-file and f-file become the main lines, White keeps d4.

approach.notes: The BDG is played by a small band of specialists; strong players seldom choose it.

level.notes: Traps and forcing early lines must be known by both sides, and the move order matters.

sublines_that_differ.name: Soller Attack
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Bf5 4. f3 Nf6 5. Bc4
sublines_that_differ.how: White develops with Bc4 and keeps the f-pawn flexible; Black has a sounder game.

character.reason: Gambit with early forcing play and traps for both sides.

gambit.reason: White offers the e-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Compensation is judged insufficient; Black has a healthy extra pawn after 4.f3 exf3.

structure.reason: The e- and f-files open straight away.

approach.reason: Seldom chosen by strong players; it scores through surprise at club level.

level.reason: Dubious gambit, so not Beginner, and the traps are known rather than deeply theoretical.

plans.reason: White sacrifices a pawn for pieces out quickly and a kingside attack.
